newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 23.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The Irish government claims that the Labour Force figures showing record job creation over the last three years supports its case for another national pay agreement.
- One hundred and fifty letters have been sent to the Irish Department of Justice to Cuban refugees telling them that their applications for asylum in Ireland have been unsuccessful.
- At the end of the inquest into the death of a 16-year-old girl at a pop concert in Dublin in May, the jury recommended that a code of practise be set up to ensure public safety at such venues.
- A big increase in the number of people employed in services and a sharp rise in the number of women at work were the main features of the Labour Force Survey released on Tuesday.
- Irish electricity supplier, ESB will receive benefits of around one million Irish pounds per annum following a leasing deal on its generating station at Moneypoint, west Ireland.

- The Russian beef ban affecting exports from counties Tipperary, Cork and Monaghan will be lifted as soon as BSE levels there fall, according to the Russian official who negotiated the deal with Ireland's Minister for Agriculture, Ivan Yates.
- The Northern Ireland peace talks can succeed without Sinn Fein, the chairman of the multi-party talks, George Mitchell, said.
- The political wing of IRA guerillas, Sinn Fein is trying to establish through behind-the-scenes contacts how the British government would respond to a IRA ceasefire, security sources said.
- The Irish gaelic games administration body, GAA handed out record player suspensions on Tuesday night following the melee which marred last month's All-Ireland football final.
- A record 488,000 Irish women are in paid employment outside the home, the Irish Labour Force Survey said.
- Irish small business representative body, ISME plans to take an action in the Irish High Court because it says it is being excluded as a full social partner in the national pay agreements.
- Dublin tops the list for fund investors putting it ahead of the Channel Islands and Guernsey, a survey by UK fund consultancy showed on Tuesday.
- London-listed exploration stock, Pan Andean Resources, which saw its share price collapse three weeks ago, is still a good speculative risk, Pan Andean chairman John Teeling said on Tuesday.
